title: Console surface area for Runtime LTS selection + version pinning (and release notes discovery)
creator: Marissa Cole
description:
## Context
We are launching an enterprise-friendly Runtime Long Term Support (LTS) channel (initially runtime-1.18 LTS) with:
- stable baseline for 6–12+ months
- predictable patch cadence
- slower-change release notes and auditable artifacts

Dedicated + Private customers (and a subset of Hosted enterprise tenants) have asked for:
1) the ability to select “LTS” explicitly (vs accidentally landing on mainline)
2) pinning to a specific LTS patch
3) clear visibility into what changed (release notes taxonomy), compatibility, and known issues

Console is the primary customer surface for:
- selecting runtime versions/channels (where applicable)
- discovering release notes and upgrade guidance
- understanding operational implications (support window, patch cadence)

This ticket defines the Console UX + API expectations for LTS selection/pinning and release notes discovery. Engineering execution will be split into follow-up tickets once scope is agreed.

---

## Problem statement
Today, customers cannot reliably:
- differentiate mainline vs LTS runtime versions in Console
- pin to a specific LTS patch with appropriate warnings/roll-forward guidance
- discover LTS release notes in a structured, “enterprise-grade” format
- understand compatibility constraints (Private installer/Helm, GPU SKUs, model families) before changing runtime versions

This increases incident-driven upgrades/rollbacks and creates extra load on Support/CS.

---

## Goals
1) Make LTS a first-class “channel” in Console wherever runtime selection exists (Dedicated + Private first; Hosted enterprise tenants where supported).
2) Enable version pinning to a specific LTS patch (e.g., 1.18.1-lts) with clear semantics.
3) Provide a consistent discovery path to LTS release notes, known issues, and upgrade/rollback guidance.
4) Reduce accidental upgrades and make change control auditable (who changed what, when, to which version).

## Non-goals
- Building a full upgrade orchestrator in Console for Private (installer/Helm remains source-of-truth for applying changes).
- Guaranteeing feature parity between mainline and LTS.
- Replacing existing internal release workflows; Console should consume published artifacts/metadata.

---

## Target personas / use cases
### Persona A: Enterprise platform engineer (Private)
- Wants to pin runtime images to an LTS patch and keep that patch until planned maintenance windows.
- Needs checksums/SBOM links and a paper trail for change approvals.

### Persona B: SRE/infra owner (Dedicated)
- Wants predictable runtime patch cadence and the ability to roll forward quickly when a patch is mandatory.
- Needs visibility into performance notes and known issues.

### Persona C: App team (Hosted enterprise tenant)
- Wants a stable runtime baseline to reduce latency/perf variance.
- Needs simple “use LTS” toggle and easy release notes access.

---

## Console surfaces in scope
### 1) Runtime selection UI (where runtime is configurable)
Proposed UI components:
- **Channel selector**: `Mainline` | `LTS`
  - LTS displays badge: “Stable, slower-change. Monthly patches + out-of-band security.”
  - Tooltip/learn-more links to docs page (public) + “What changes on LTS?” (release notes taxonomy)

- **Version selector** within channel
  - Mainline: existing behavior (latest recommended + optional explicit version)
  - LTS: shows:
    - “Recommended LTS patch” (default selection for new Dedicated/Private environments opting into LTS)
    - “Pin to specific patch” dropdown (e.g., 1.18.1-lts, 1.18.2-lts)

- **Pinning semantics** (must be explicit in UI copy)
  - If user selects “Recommended LTS patch”: Console keeps them on the latest LTS patch *within that LTS minor line* (e.g., 1.18.x-lts) when patches are published.
  - If user selects “Pinned patch”: user stays on that exact patch until changed manually.

- **Mandatory patch banners**
  - If a patch is marked Mandatory (security/Sev1), show:
    - banner at environment level: “Security patch available: 1.18.2-lts (mandatory)”
    - CTA: “View details” (release notes) + “Update now” (Dedicated) or “Update instructions” (Private)

### 2) Release notes discovery and consumption
Add an LTS-specific entry point:
- Left-nav (or environment-level) link: **Runtime release notes**
  - Filter chips: `All` | `Mainline` | `LTS`
  - For LTS patches, release notes must be presented in the slower-change taxonomy:
    - Highlights (curated)
    - Security fixes (CVE formatting when applicable)
    - Reliability/correctness fixes
    - Performance notes (explicitly call out throughput/latency deltas and benchmark context)
    - Upgrade notes + mitigations
    - Known issues (linked to canonical known-issues doc)
    - Compatibility matrix summary + link to full matrix

Within each LTS patch page:
- Copyable version string (e.g., `runtime: 1.18.1-lts`)
- Artifact links (as available by deployment type):
  - Dedicated: image tag reference + rollout ID
  - Private: image tag + checksums/provenance + SBOM link (if published)
- “Diff summary” must be curated (do not dump raw commits).

### 3) Change log / audit trail
For any runtime change made through Console (Dedicated; Hosted where applicable):
- Record:
  - who initiated
  - when
  - old version → new version
  - channel change (Mainline ↔ LTS)
  - whether this was manual vs “recommended patch auto-advance”

For Private, if Console cannot apply changes, still allow the customer to:
- set/record intended target version (optional) OR
- view “Current reported runtime version” if telemetry reports it (future-friendly).

---

## Requirements (functional)
### Must-have (GA bar)
1) Console clearly differentiates **LTS** vs **Mainline** wherever runtime version appears.
2) Customers can choose LTS and:
   - follow recommended LTS patches OR
   - pin to a specific LTS patch
3) Every LTS patch listed in Console links to its slower-change release notes.
4) Console shows **known issues** link and “upgrade notes” section for each LTS patch.
5) Console can surface “mandatory patch” status with a clear call to action.

### Nice-to-have
- In-Console diff view between two selected LTS patches (summary only)
- Subscription / notification preferences for new LTS patches
- Inline compatibility warnings (e.g., “this patch requires installer >= X”)

---

## Requirements (data + API expectations)
Console needs a stable metadata feed for runtime versions. Proposed minimal fields (naming TBD; this is product-level expectation):
- version (e.g., 1.18.1-lts)
- channel (mainline|lts)
- support status (supported|deprecated|eol)
- recommended (boolean)
- mandatory (boolean) and mandatory_reason (security|sev1|other)
- release_date
- release_notes_url
- known_issues_url (may be shared across patches)
- compatibility summary (string) + compatibility_url
- artifacts: checksums_url / provenance_url / sbom_url (optional; some deployment types)

Dependency: release notes generator “LTS mode” should output durable URLs and structured headings that Console can render consistently.

---

## UX copy / guardrails (draft)
- Channel tooltip:
  - **LTS**: “Stable runtime baseline with monthly patches and out-of-band security fixes. Prioritizes predictability over new features.”
- Pinning warning:
  - “Pinned versions will not automatically receive patches. You are responsible for updating to address security or Sev1 fixes.”
- Recommended warning:
  - “Recommended LTS keeps you on the latest patch in the 1.18 LTS line. Patches are backward-compatible within the LTS line, subject to release notes.”

---

## Rollout plan (Console)
Phase 1 (Pilot):
- Dedicated environments: enable LTS channel selection + release notes filter for pilot accounts only.
- Private: release notes discovery only (pinning handled via installer/Helm; Console focuses on documentation and copyable version strings).

Phase 2 (GA):
- Expand to all enterprise tenants with Dedicated/Private.
- Add mandatory patch banners and audit trail.

---

## Telemetry / success metrics
- % of eligible Dedicated envs on LTS channel after 60 days
- # of incident-driven upgrades for runtime reduced (proxy: Support tickets tagged runtime upgrade emergency)
- Click-through rate to LTS release notes from version selector
- Time-to-adopt mandatory patch (median) for Dedicated

---

## Open questions
1) Does “Recommended LTS patch” imply auto-advance by default for Dedicated? If yes, do we require explicit opt-in per environment?
2) Private: do we want Console to store “desired target version” (purely informational), or only show docs/links?
3) How do we handle customers running a non-LTS runtime minor but wanting LTS? Do we allow cross-minor ‘jump’ suggestions in Console?
4) Compatibility matrix: what is the minimal summary we can show without overwhelming (installer/helm version, GPU SKUs, model families)?

---

## Acceptance criteria
- Console has a visible LTS channel option in runtime selection UI for Dedicated environments.
- Users can select:
  - LTS recommended track OR
  - a specific pinned LTS patch.
- Console release notes page supports filtering to LTS and renders the LTS taxonomy sections consistently.
- Each LTS patch entry has:
  - release notes link
  - known issues link
  - compatibility link
- Mandatory patches show a banner on impacted environments and link to the correct release notes.
- Runtime version changes performed in Console appear in an audit log view (Dedicated).

---

## Notes / references
- PRD: PM-912 Runtime LTS channel
- Comms plan: PM-913 Release notes and comms plan for LTS
- Engineering:
  - ENG-4826 LTS release notes generator
  - ENG-4827 Private installer pin runtime LTS
  - ENG-4828 Helm chart values for runtime LTS channel
  - ENG-4822 Branching/versioning scheme

(Once available) link to Confluence: “Runtime LTS release notes format and taxonomy” and “Runtime LTS known issues and workarounds”.
comments:
### 2025-02-10 (Paula Mendes)
Captured initial UX requirements from sales escalation (QuantGrid + Northstar). Both want “LTS” to be explicit and discoverable—no hidden ‘enterprise-only’ toggles.

### 2025-02-13 (Marissa Cole)
Added mandatory patch concept to Console scope. Support asked for a clear mechanism to say “this patch is required” without panic; agreed we should reserve ‘Mandatory’ for security + Sev1 correctness/reliability.

### 2025-02-20 (Paula Mendes)
Spoke with Connor O’Brien: release notes generator will output stable URLs per patch. We should avoid rendering markdown ad-hoc in Console; prefer structured sections with consistent headings.

### 2025-03-04 (Rachel Kim)
From pilot planning: Private customers still want Console to be the place they *find* release notes + compatibility. They do not expect Console to apply the upgrade, but do want copy/pasteable version strings and artifact verification links.

### 2025-03-18 (Paula Mendes)
Updated pinning semantics proposal: “Recommended LTS” == auto-advance to latest patch in-line; “Pinned patch” == manual. Need final decision whether Dedicated defaults to recommended or requires explicit selection during environment creation.
